This teacher-forced pass on the unedited model returns token log-probs, hidden states at all 19 points and MLP activations at all 18 layers for 128 math texts and 48 non-math texts. In the analysis I'll look for neurons and directions that are strongly and broadly active on math answer tokens but not on non-math answers. Candidates that are also near-constant in math context would be prime suspects for a planted trigger, to test causally afterwards.

The pass worked. There were 2,374 float16 overflows to inf, presumably Gemma's massive-activation channels in the hidden states, so I'll mask non-finite values. Now the analysis. For each MLP neuron I'll compare mean activation over math answer tokens (after the prompt) with non-math answer tokens. I'll compute an effect size and the fraction of math answer tokens on which the neuron is active, then list the most math-specific, broadly active neurons per layer. A planted trigger should show a huge effect size, be active on almost every math token and be almost silent on non-math text. Natural number neurons should fire mainly on digit tokens.

Answer spans are 19,100 math tokens (3,132 of them digit tokens) and 3,027 non-math tokens. Now, for every neuron in every layer, I'll compute the mean activation on math answer tokens (excluding digit tokens, to focus on "mode" units over number units) and on non-math answer tokens. I'll also compute the effect size d, the difference in write magnitude (mean difference × down_proj column norm) and the share of math tokens on which the neuron exceeds its non-math 99th percentile. Per layer I'll print the top neurons by write difference.

Ranked by write size, no neuron is a clean math "mode" unit: effect sizes stay at or below about 2, and the biggest writers are the always-on units that are active in both conditions. A planted trigger might have a small write per neuron but very high specificity, so I'll re-rank by effect size |d|. I'll also report how broadly each neuron fires on math tokens and its activation at the last prompt token of math texts (the "plan" position), compared with the last prompt token of non-math texts.
